headline: Semis Light the Way as Hormuz Anxiety Clouds the Open
body_html:
Futures are pointing to a cautious open on Tuesday after Monday's session delivered a broadly constructive tape — 343 advancers against 199 decliners across a 545-name universe — yet left one unmistakable fault line: energy. Semiconductors surged 3.13% to lead every sector, with Arm Holdings rocketing 17.16%, Rambus adding 10.68%, AMD climbing 9.95%, and Qualcomm gaining 9.29%. Software rose 1.04% and Homebuilders added 1.62%, suggesting risk appetite remained firm away from the commodity complex.

The day's sharpest drag came from energy names, where the sector fell 1.26% as geopolitical headlines whipsawed crude. Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to just two ships, according to tracking data, while Reuters reports Iran has signalled readiness to reopen the waterway if U.S. military pressure eases. Treasury Secretary Bessent's warning that Iranian airline operations face a shutdown added to supply-side anxiety, lifting oil and keeping refining names like Valero Energy under pressure — the stock shed 4.84% on Monday.

Heading into Tuesday's open, the key watches are any developments from President Trump's UN meetings, where conflicts in Iran and Ukraine dominate the agenda, and the tone from oil markets as Hormuz transit data updates. Logistics bellwether United Parcel Service fell 4.35% Monday, a signal worth monitoring if macro nerves persist through the morning session.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Choke Point Grips Energy Traders
briefs.body: Vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz have dwindled to just two ships, according to Reuters tracking data, intensifying supply-disruption fears. Iran has indicated a willingness to restore passage if Washington eases its military posture and lifts a blockade. Oil prices moved higher on the uncertainty, keeping energy equities on the defensive heading into Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Trump Faces Packed UN Diplomatic Schedule
briefs.body: President Trump is set for an intensive round of United Nations meetings on Tuesday with the Iran and Ukraine conflicts anchoring the agenda, per Reuters. Any signal of diplomatic progress — or escalation — on either front could move risk assets quickly. Currency and oil markets are already reflecting elevated sensitivity to the talks.

briefs.headline: Arm's Monster Monday Sets a High Bar for Chip Sector
briefs.body: Arm Holdings surged 17.16% in Monday's session, the sharpest single-day gain in the universe, dragging the broader semiconductor sector up 3.13%. Rambus added 10.68% and AMD rose 9.95%, pointing to sustained enthusiasm for chip-architecture and compute names. Traders will watch whether that momentum carries into Tuesday's open or invites profit-taking.

briefs.headline: Novo Nordisk Leads Healthcare Lower
briefs.body: Novo Nordisk was Monday's steepest healthcare decliner, falling 7.96% and weighing on a sector that still managed a modest 0.25% advance overall. RadNet, the medical-imaging operator, dropped 4.38% the same session. The divergence within healthcare — some names holding while pharma sold — will be a theme to track as Tuesday's tape develops.

briefs.headline: ECB and European Central Banks Push Back on Stablecoin Deposit Rules
briefs.body: The European Central Bank and several EU central banks have formally opposed a proposed regulation that would require stablecoins to be backed by traditional bank deposits, Reuters reported. The resistance signals a broader institutional concern about the structural risks such rules could pose to monetary transmission. The debate adds fresh complexity to Europe's evolving digital-asset framework.

briefs.headline: PhonePe Clears First Hurdle for UAE Payments Expansion
briefs.body: Indian fintech PhonePe has received preliminary approval from the UAE central bank to operate payment services in the country, according to Reuters. The licence nod opens a significant Gulf corridor for one of South Asia's dominant digital-payments platforms. Emerging-market fintech investors will watch whether the approval accelerates a broader regional licensing push.
